expectations.text: A manifest/registry file is actually created on disk (not just described in the chat response)
expectations.evidence: File exists on disk: outputs/assets/MANIFEST.md, containing Characters/Locations/Props tables with Tag, File, Critical details, and Status columns.

expectations.text: Each of the three elements is assigned an @tag-style reference name (short, lowercase, prompt-ready)
expectations.evidence: MANIFEST.md assigns '@mom', '@kitchen', '@pan_arrow' — all short, lowercase, prompt-ready.

expectations.text: All three asset filenames (mom_sheet_v2.png, kitchen_v1.png, pan_v3_arrow.png) are recorded with paths
expectations.evidence: Recorded with full relative paths: 'assets/characters/mom_sheet_v2.png', 'assets/locations/kitchen_v1.png', 'assets/props/pan_v3_arrow.png'; response instructs the user to move the images to these locations.

expectations.text: Critical visible details are captured per element: red polka dot apron + round glasses for Mom, red arrow at the handle grip for the pan
expectations.evidence: Mom's Critical details: 'red polka dot apron, round glasses'; pan's: 'red arrow points at the handle grip'.

expectations.text: Registered elements carry a status (e.g., final) distinguishing accepted assets from drafts
expectations.evidence: Status column shows 'final' for all three; response explains 'All three assets are marked final since you approved them... safe to reference in video prompts immediately.'

suggestions.reason: The kitchen entry's Critical details cell is '—' (empty). No assertion checks that the manifest captures details only when they exist / handles detail-less assets, but more importantly nothing checks that the manifest's paths point at real files — both runs record paths to images that were never moved. Consider an assertion about how missing files are handled or flagged.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions pass with substantive evidence; the file-on-disk requirement was the right call and both configurations satisfied it.
